agent: land orders wave, reader A (the window)
question: The land orders window (land_unit_order, CLandOrdersView): its constructor, which orders it lists and which it ticks, AddOrder, the radio group, Update, accept and cancel, the date widget, sync_checkbox and sync_title, the daytime row, the tooltips, and the key that opens it.

structs.name: CLandOrdersView
structs.comment: **The land orders window** (`land_unit_order` of interface/orders.gui), a COrdersView of mode 2 (slot 1 is the shared `mov eax, 2; ret`). Made by CInGameIdler::OpenOrdersView with Ctrl and a right click on a province for a land unit, for the first selected unit. Holds the unit (a CRef at +0x0C), the province (+0x34), the window (+0x08), the three orders it made (+0x3C), the date widget (+0xA4/+0xA8), the radio group of the rows (by value at +0xAC, its ticked checkbox at +0x140) and the rows' checkboxes (+0x15C). Three CButtonObserverGlue<CLandOrdersView> (vftable 0x15D7468) sit at +0x4C (accept -> CLandOrdersView::OnAccept), +0x78 (cancel -> OrdersView_Cancel) and +0x16C (-> CLandOrdersView::ClearUnitOrder, wired to nothing), and a CRadioButtonGroupObserverGlue<CLandOrdersView> (0x15D7494) at +0x150 whose handler is the shared empty stub 0xABF890. No stance, no priority, nothing remembered between windows. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
structs.evidence: Size from `push 0x198; call operator_new` at 0x6772B2 before `call 0x73C270` at 0x6772D7 in CInGameIdler::OpenOrdersView's mode-2 arm. vftable 0x15D7448 written at 0x73C2A1 and is the RTTI export's CLandOrdersView table (7 slots, base COrdersView at 0). The glue vftables are the RTTI's VCLandOrdersView::__CButtonObserverGlue (0x15D7468) and __CRadioButtonGroupObserverGlue (0x15D7494). inherits is omitted because COrdersView has no struct record; wrong if the size were not 0x198 - the dtor's last field touched is +0x16C's glue and the ctor zeroes up to +0x194.

struct_fields.name: idler
struct_fields.comment: The in-game screen that opened it; its selection (+0x1304) is what AddOrder tests and OnAccept posts for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Ctor stores its second argument here at 0x73C2A7; CInGameIdler::OpenOrdersView passes the idler there (0x6772D0/0x6772D5). AddOrder 0x73CEF8 and OnAccept 0x73D811 read [+4]+0x1304, the recorded CInGameIdler selection.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The window `land_unit_order`, made by the gui factory's slot 11 by name. Every element is looked up through it; its CGuiObject at +0x18 is what IsShown (+0x5B) and IsUnderPointer (slot 37) ask. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: `push 'land_unit_order'` at 0x73C3DB, the factory call at 0x73C41D, stored at 0x73C428. Update looks up sync_checkbox, daytime_title, daytime_icon, daytime_icondesc, accept and sync_title through [+8]; slot 3 0x73D8C0 is `mov eax,[ecx+8]; mov al,[eax+0x5B]`.

struct_fields.name: unit
struct_fields.comment: The unit the window was opened for (the first selected), as a CRef by persistent id. The three orders are made for it; OnAccept and ClearUnitOrder resolve it first and do nothing where it is gone. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Ctor 0x73C298..0x73C2AA: `lea ecx,[ebx+0xc]; push unit; push ecx; call 0x42DD70` - 0x42DD70 is the CRef builder (CMoveCommand, CAssignLeaderCommand use it the same way). OnAccept 0x73D786 and 0x73D8F3 pass `lea esi,[this+0xc]` to CRef_ResolveAndCache (0x42DE10). The dtor frees a string at +0x18..+0x2C, the CRef's name. Wrong if CRef were not 0x28 bytes: +0x34 is the next field written.

struct_fields.name: province
struct_fields.comment: The province right-clicked: its name is the title and the daytime line, it is the target of the three orders, and its id goes in every command accept posts. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: Ctor stores its fourth argument at 0x73C2B2; title from [+0x34]+8 slot 7 at 0x73C74B; Update passes it to IsNight in EDI at 0x73D012; OnAccept pushes [[+0x34]+0xD0] (the province id) at 0x73D85E. Already read as +0x34 by LandOrdersView_EstimateArrival.

struct_fields.name: open
struct_fields.comment: Set at the end of the constructor; OnAccept and cancel (OrdersView_Cancel) clear it, and Update returns it, which is how the window is closed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov byte ptr [ebx+0x38],1` at 0x73C90B; `mov byte ptr [ebx+0x38],0` at 0x73D8A4 (OnAccept) and 0x742A90 (the cancel glue's handler); Update ends `mov al,[ebx+0x38]; ret` at 0x73D446. The air view has the same byte at the same offset (CAirOrdersView +0x38 `open`).

struct_fields.name: orders
struct_fields.comment: The orders the constructor made, one per row, appended by AddOrder: a CMoveOrder, a CSupportAttackOrder and a CStrategicRedeploymentOrder, in that order. Kept only for their slot 11 at opening; destroyed with the view. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: AddOrder 0x73CBC9..0x73CC01 appends a 0x10-byte node {order, prev=tail, next=0} with tail +0x40, count +0x44, head +0x3C; the dtor passes &+0x3C to CListOfOwned_ClearByPointer (0x4B6260) at 0x73C98B. The ctor zeroes +0x3C..+0x44 and the no-unlink byte +0x48.

struct_fields.name: date_widget_window
struct_fields.comment: The window made from `datewidget` (interface/datewidget.gui), placed at the positionType `land_mission_timewidget_start` (x 50, y 200) and added to the land window as the child `start_widget`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: `push 'datewidget'` at 0x73C4E4, the factory's slot 11 at 0x73C596, stored at 0x73C5A0; `push 'land_mission_timewidget_start'` at 0x73C670 and its +0x64/+0x68 pushed to [+0xA4] slot 42 at 0x73C6D4..0x73C6DC; `push 'start_widget'` at 0x73C6E5 with [+0xA4] to the window's slot 47 at 0x73C716.

struct_fields.name: date_widget
struct_fields.comment: The date widget (0x16C bytes, DateWidget_Construct): its date (+0x160) starts at the hour now, is shown by DateWidget_ShowDate, is raised by Update to the synchronised arrival, and is what OnAccept sends as the hour before which the unit does not move. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: `push 0x16c; call operator_new` at 0x73C5B4, DateWidget_Construct with ECX = [+0xA4] at 0x73C5D3, stored at 0x73C5E0; `mov edx,[gamestate+0xBDC]; mov [ecx+0x160],edx; call DateWidget_ShowDate` at 0x73C65D..0x73C669. Update reads and raises [+0xA8]+0x160 at 0x73CFF5 and 0x73D42A..0x73D441; OnAccept reads it at 0x73D7CF.

struct_fields.name: ticked_checkbox
struct_fields.comment: The +0x94 of the radio group held by value at +0xAC: the checkbox of the row ticked, or null. Its name (+8) is the order's token key - `move_order`, `support_attack`, `strategic_redeployment` - which OnAccept turns back into the order's type. Update greys accept while it is null. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: The radio group's select-by-name (0xAD53E0) stores the checkbox it ticks at group+0x94 (0xAD5467) and the group is at view+0xAC (ctor 0x73C34C; 0xAD53E0 called with EDI = view+0xAC at 0x73C8E4), so +0x140. LandOrdersView_IsMoveOrder compares [[+0x140]+8] with 'move_order'; OnAccept looks [[+0x140]+8] up in g_dynamic_tokens at 0x73D79E..0x73D7C3; Update tests [+0x140] at 0x73D27A. AddOrder sets each checkbox's name to the order's TokenText (checkbox slot 30 at 0x73CED4) before adding it to the group (slot 44, 0x73CEA9).

struct_fields.name: checkboxes
struct_fields.comment: The rows' checkboxes, one per order in the order of the rows, appended by AddOrder; emptied by the destructor. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
struct_fields.evidence: AddOrder 0x73CD2D..0x73CD87 appends a node {checkbox, prev=tail, next=0}, tail +0x160, count +0x164, head +0x15C; the dtor walks and frees it at 0x73C9E8..0x73CA2E and zeroes the three dwords.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::CLandOrdersView
addresses.signature: CLandOrdersView* __stdcall CLandOrdersView::CLandOrdersView(CLandOrdersView* this, CInGameIdler* idler, CUnit* unit, CMapProvince* province)
addresses.comment: **Makes the land orders window.** 0x73C270..0x73C91D, `ret 0x10`, one caller (CInGameIdler::OpenOrdersView, mode 2). Keeps the idler (+4), the unit as a CRef (+0x0C) and the province (+0x34); makes the window `land_unit_order` (+8); wires `accept` to CLandOrdersView::OnAccept and `cancel` to OrdersView_Cancel; makes the radio group (+0xAC). Makes a `datewidget` window (+0xA4) and a date widget (+0xA8) whose date is **the hour now** (CCurrentGameState +0xBDC), placed at `land_mission_timewidget_start` and attached as `start_widget`. Writes the province's name into `title`. Then three orders for the unit and the province, each handed to CLandOrdersView::AddOrder in this order - **CMoveOrder** (0x1836A0), **CSupportAttackOrder** (built inline, 0x38 bytes, `combat` +0x34 false), **CStrategicRedeploymentOrder** (0x183790) - and ticks one by name: `support_attack` where AddOrder said it may be given, else `move_order` where it may, else `strategic_redeployment` where it may, else nothing. The window is shown (its CGuiObject's slot 13) and `open` (+0x38) set. Nothing is restored from an earlier window. The name is RTTI's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing. The three allocations: `push 0x34` 0x73C7CC + `call 0x5836A0` 0x73C7E1 (writes vftable 0x15C59BC, CMoveOrder, at 0x5836F9); `push 0x38` 0x73C7F1 with the inline COrder base and vftable 0x15C5A4C (CSupportAttackOrder) at 0x73C857; `push 0x34` 0x73C86C + `call 0x583790` (vftable 0x15C5ADC, CStrategicRedeploymentOrder, at 0x5837E9). Each result is `push eax; push ebx; call 0x73CBA0` (0x73C7EC, 0x73C867, 0x73C88C), the answers kept in [ebp+0x17], [ebp+0xF] and AL. The tick ladder 0x73C891..0x73C8EA tests them in the order support, move, redeploy and passes the string to the radio group's select-by-name 0xAD53E0. Wrong if 0xAD53E0 were not a select: it sets the found checkbox's +0x60 (ticked) to 1 and group+0x94 to it (0xAD544B..0xAD5467).

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 0: CLandOrdersView::~CLandOrdersView, then `free` where bit 0 of the flags is set. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73C920..0x73C93E: `call 0x73C950; test byte [ebp+8],1; je; push esi; call 0xB95F9B`, `ret 4`. The RTTI export lists 0x73C920 as CLandOrdersView slot 0 and vtable.py --holding finds it in that table alone.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::~CLandOrdersView
addresses.comment: Closes the window (its slot 20), destroys the three orders (CListOfOwned_ClearByPointer on +0x3C), frees the date widget (+0xA8, its eight button glues reset first), clears the radio group (its slot 45) and the checkbox list (+0x15C), resets the glues and the unit's CRef, and leaves the COrdersView vftable. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73C950..0x73CAF0: [+8] slot 20 at 0x73C985; `push &+0x3C; call 0x4B6260` at 0x73C98B; +0xA8's +0x2C..+0x134 reset to the CButtonObserver vftable and freed at 0x73C99F..0x73C9CB; [+0xAC] slot 45 at 0x73C9E6; the +0x15C walk; vftable 0x15D7428 (COrdersView) written at 0x73CADE. Called only by slot 0.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::AddOrder
addresses.comment: **Makes a row for an order, whether or not it can be given.** Appends the order to +0x3C; makes an `order_entry` window as a list entry, writes the order's slot 6 (its name key, MOVE_ORDER / SUPPORT_ATTACK / ORDER_STRATEGIC_REDEPLOYMENT) into its `name`, appends it to `orders_list`; its `checkbox` goes on +0x15C, is renamed to the order's token key (TokenText of slot 16) and added to the radio group under that name. Then for **every** thing in the selection (CInGameIdler +0x1304) the order's unit (+8) is set to it and the order's slot 11 (MayBeGiven) asked: **one no greys the row** (checkbox +0x136 cleared), all yes leaves it enabled; the answer is whether all said yes. Unlike CNavalOrdersView::AddOrder there is no range test and no name-to-order map. Runs only from the constructor, so a row's greying is fixed when the window opens. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73CBA0..0x73CF78, `ret 8`, three callers all in the constructor (0x73C7EC, 0x73C867, 0x73C88C). 'order_entry' 0x73CC20, 'checkbox' 0x73CCE2 (row slot 18), 'name' 0x73CD8F with order slot 6 (+0x18) at 0x73CDC2 and GuiObject_textBoxType::SetText 0x73CDD9, 'orders_list' 0x73CE22 then list slot 4 (row, 1) at 0x73CE5D; TokenText (0xA6A230) of slot 16 pushed to the group's slot 44 at 0x73CEA9 and to the checkbox's slot 30 at 0x73CED4. The selection loop 0x73CF20..0x73CF3C stores [node] at order+8 and calls slot 11 (+0x2C); 0x73CF43 clears +0x136 where any failed, 0x73CF53 sets it to 1 where all passed and it was 0, then 0xA81AA0(checkbox); `sete al` on the failure flag at 0x73CF6A.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 2, each frame. (1) g_LandOrdersSyncArrival = `sync_checkbox` ticked (+0x60 == 1). (2) The day or night **at the date widget's hour**: the widget's date turned into a month and an hour of the day (days / 365.0, then MonthLengthTable) and IsNight(province, hour, month); `daytime_title` = ORDER_DAY_TIME with PROV the province's name ("Locally in Reppen:"), `daytime_icon` frame 2 at night and 1 by day, `daytime_icondesc` ORDER_NIGHT or ORDER_DAY. (3) `accept` enabled (slot 46) while a row is ticked (+0x140), else disabled (47). (4) **`sync_checkbox` and `sync_title` are shown only while the ticked row is `move_order`** (slots 13 and 14). (5) With `move_order` ticked and the sync box ticked, LandOrdersView_EstimateArrival, and the widget's date raised to it where it is later - never lowered. Returns `open` (+0x38). Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73CF80..0x73D458, the RTTI's CLandOrdersView slot 2. 'sync_checkbox' 0x73CFA3 and `cmp [eax+0x60],1; sete cl; mov [0x1A8560A],cl` 0x73CFCF..0x73CFE1; the date arithmetic 0x73CFF5..0x73D058 (`add eax,0xFD63AA40` = minus the 43800000 epoch, idiv 24, g_DaysPerYear 0x160A550, MonthLengthTable 0x1713294) into `call 0x4A7390` (IsNight) with EDI = +0x34; ORDER_DAY_TIME/PROV through AppendLocalisedLine 0x73D0B1; icon slot 18 with `setne cl; inc ecx` 0x73D184..0x73D190; ORDER_NIGHT/ORDER_DAY 0x73D1AE..0x73D1B5 through LocaliseKeyToString; accept slot 46/47 on [+0x140] 0x73D27A..0x73D2CC; LandOrdersView_IsMoveOrder 0x73D2E7 choosing slot 13 (Show) or 14 (Hide) for both elements; 0x73D40D..0x73D441 the raise with `jle`. Wrong if slot 13/14 of a CGuiObject were not Show/Hide - the record has them so (CTopBar slot 2, CProductionView).

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::OnAccept
addresses.comment: **`accept`.** Where the view's unit still exists and a row is ticked: the order's type is the ticked checkbox's name looked up in g_dynamic_tokens (0xC where absent); the two dates are (the date widget's date, the null date), or - with `move_order` ticked and the sync box ticked - (the null date, LandOrdersView_EstimateArrival). Then for every thing of the selection that is a land unit (slot 15) and is not retreating (CUnit +0x158), a CSetOrderCommand(unit, type, the province's id, first date, second date), posted through the in-game screen's command channel (slot 18, +0x38, slot 6). CSetOrderCommand::Execute puts the first date on the unit's move_not_before (+0xCC) and the second on its end_date (+0xD0): **without sync the order does not start before the widget's hour; with it, every unit starts now and arrives no earlier than the slowest's estimated arrival**. No stance is set, so the command keeps its constructor's 1 (defensive) and stop -1000. Then `open` is cleared, which closes the window. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73D760..0x73D8B4, reached only through the glue at +0x4C (handler stored at 0x73C2CC; findValue finds that one reference). CRef_ResolveAndCache of +0x0C 0x73D789; TernarySearchTreeFind on 0x1710DF0 0x73D7B8, default `mov [ebp-0x18],0xC` 0x73D7C8; dates [ebp-0x14]/[ebp-0x10] = widget +0x160 / g_NullDate 0x73D7CF..0x73D7E5, swapped to g_NullDate / estimate at 0x73D7FF..0x73D80E under IsMoveOrder and [0x1A8560A]; the loop 0x73D822..0x73D89E with unit slot 15 (+0x3C) and `cmp byte [edi+0x158],0`; `push 0xA0; call operator_new` and CSetOrderCommand's constructor 0x5E1E70 with (unit, type, [[+0x34]+0xD0], [ebp-0x14], [ebp-0x10]); the constructor stores them at +0x64, +0x68, +0x6C, +0x70 and stance +0x94 = 1, stop +0x9C = -1000 (0x5E1F00..0x5E1F68); Execute stores +0x6C/+0x70 into CUnit +0xCC/+0xD0 at 0x5E2015/0x5E201B.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::IsShown
addresses.comment: Slot 3: the window's shown byte, `[[this+8]+0x5B]` (the CGuiObject at +0x18, its +0x43). The input handler asks it before handing a right click on the map to slot 4, which for this view is the shared `ret 8` (0xA806D0) - so with the land window up a right click on the map does nothing, as with the naval one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73D8C0..0x73D8C6: `mov eax,[ecx+8]; mov al,[eax+0x5B]; ret`. CLandOrdersView slot 3 in the RTTI export and in vtable.py, alone; slot 4 of the table is 0xA806D0, the recorded shared stub.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::ClearUnitOrder
addresses.comment: The handler of the glue at +0x16C, which **nothing wires to a button**: where the view's unit exists, has an order (CUnit +0xB0) and that order's slot 24 answers yes, it posts CSetOrderCommand(unit, 0x18D - the null order -, 1, now, now). The same body as the air view's unwired glue at +0x350 (0x747410). Dead in this view as far as found. Bare `ret`. The name is ours (inferred: what posting a null order with both dates now is for was not read). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x73D8D0..0x73DB4F, bare `ret`. Unit resolved by CRef_ResolveAndCache (0x73D8FA) and FindPersistentById with the 0x1268 split (0x73D91D..0x73D932); `cmp [eax+0xB0],0` 0x73D942; order slot 24 (+0x60) 0x73D960; `push now; push now; push 1; push 0x18D; unit; this` into 0x5E1E70 at 0x73DA6C..0x73DA95; posted by in_game_screen slot 18, +0x38, slot 6. findValue(0x73D8D0) has one hit, the ctor's store at 0x73C3A1; no `lea` of +0x16C anywhere in the view (the same search finds the accept and cancel glues' `lea eax,[ebx+0x4C]`/`[ebx+0x78]` at 0x73C471/0x73C4C4). Wrong if something outside the view registers view+0x16C - not searched image-wide.

addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::IsUnderPointer
addresses.comment: Slot 5: a tail jump to the window's CGuiObject (+0x18) slot 37 with the caller's argument - whether the pointer is over the window. Unlike the air view it asks no date window separately (the date widget is a child of this window). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x747690..0x7476A3: `mov ecx,[ecx+8]; mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; add ecx,0x18; mov eax,[eax+0x94]; pop ebp; jmp eax`. CLandOrdersView slot 5 alone (vtable.py --holding). addresses.name: CLandOrdersView::GetTooltip
addresses.signature: void* __thiscall CLandOrdersView::GetTooltip(CLandOrdersView* this, void* out, void* element)
addresses.comment: Slot 6. **Only the daytime row has a tooltip**: for `daytime_title`, `daytime_icon` or `daytime_icondesc`, ORDER_DAY_TIME_DESC ("Estimated local day time in PROV when the mission begins is: TIME") with PROV the province's name and TIME ORDER_NIGHT or ORDER_DAY at the date widget's hour, worked out as in Update. Every other element - the rows, accept, cancel, the sync box, the date widget - gets the empty answer, so unlike the naval and air views a row shows no description. `ret 8`, returns `out`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x7476B0..0x7478DF, CLandOrdersView slot 6 alone. `out` initialised at 0x7476DD..0x747704; element slot 17 (name) compared with 'daytime_title' 0x74771F, 'daytime_icon' 0x74775F and String_EqualsCString 'daytime_icondesc' 0x747797, the last failing to 0x7478CD (return); the date arithmetic and IsNight 0x7477A9..0x74780C; 'ORDER_DAY_TIME_DESC' with 'PROV' and 'TIME' through AppendLocalisedLine2 (0x4735D0) at 0x747862. Wrong if another layer answered for the rows - not looked for.

addresses.name: OrdersView_Cancel
addresses.comment: **`cancel` of the air and the land orders windows**: `mov byte [ecx+0x38],0; ret` - clears `open`, which closes the window. Held by the cancel glue at +0x78 of both CAirOrdersView (0x740157) and CLandOrdersView (0x73C2F5); in no virtual table. Class-free because two classes' glues share it (the naval view has its own, 0x73EC30, its `open` being +0x30). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: Five bytes then `int3`. findValue(0x742A90) answers the two glue stores; vtable.py --holding: in no table. Both classes' `open` is +0x38 (CAirOrdersView +0x38 recorded; the land ctor sets it at 0x73C90B). FINDINGS-airorders.md section 12 had it 'taken to close the window' unread.

addresses.name: DateWidget_Construct
addresses.comment: Builds a date widget (0x16C bytes) over a `datewidget` window: eight CButtonObserverGlue<CDateWidget> (vftable 0x15CAE1C) wired to `year_up`, `year_down`, `month_up`, `month_down`, `day_up`, `day_down`, `hour_up` and `hour_down` (DateWidget_YearUp .. DateWidget_HourDown), the date (+0x160) set to the null date, the window kept at +0x164, and the buttons switched on (+0x168 = 1). `ret 4`, returns the widget. Callers: CLandOrdersView's constructor and CAirOrdersView's (twice). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.evidence: 0x60E000..0x60E644 `ret 4`; the object is [ebp+8] (esi, returned), the window ECX stored at +0x164 at 0x60E235; handlers 0x60E650..0x60E8C0 stored at +0x08, +0x34(edi+8), +0x60, +0x8C, +0xB8, +0xE4, +0x110, +0x13C; the eight button names pushed from 0x60E23B to 0x60E4F8; `mov byte [esi+0x168],1` 0x60E243. findRefs --callers: 0x73C5D3, 0x740DE7, 0x740E8F.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OpenOrdersView
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CInGameIdler::OpenOrdersView(int mode@ECX, CInGameIdler* idler@EDX, CInGameIdler* owner@stack:4, CUnit* unit@stack:8, CMapProvince* province@stack:12)
addresses.comment: **Opens the window of orders a right click with a fleet or an air unit, or Ctrl and a right click with a land unit, brings up.** Nothing where the view at idler +0x160 is already of this mode (its slot 1); otherwise the old view is closed and a new one made: mode 0 a CNavalOrdersView (0x274 bytes), 1 a CAirOrdersView (0x37C), 2 a CLandOrdersView (0x198). CUnit::OrderToProvince calls it with 0 for a fleet clicked without shift, 1 for an air unit, 2 for a land unit with **Ctrl** held (the keyboard's slot 12, Keyboard_IsCtrlDown; FINDINGS-selection.md section A). Only an air window has the last one's settings restored (0x747300); a land window starts fresh each time. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 1, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
addresses.revises: The comment said mode 2 came 'under a key not identified'; FINDINGS-selection.md section A settled it as Ctrl (keyboard slot 12, [+0x51] VK_CONTROL) and the call site 0x5C2497..0x5C24B2 tests [unit's idler+0x1C] slot 12 (+0x30) directly before `mov ecx,2; call`. Also adds that only mode 1 restores settings (`cmp eax,1` at 0x67734E before 0x747300).
addresses.evidence: 0x5C2497: `mov ecx,[esi+0x1C]; call [eax+0x30]; test al,al; je` then `mov ecx,2; mov edx,esi; call 0x677260` at 0x5C24AB..0x5C24B2. In 0x677260 the mode-2 arm 0x6772B2..0x6772DC calls 0x73C270, and the restore 0x747300 runs only where the new view's slot 1 answers 1 (0x67734C..0x67735F).

addresses.comment: Whether the land orders window's ticked row is `move_order`: the radio group's ticked checkbox (CLandOrdersView +0x140) has the name `move_order` (String_Equals on its name at +8), the name AddOrder gave it from the order's token; false with nothing ticked. Called by CLandOrdersView::Update (twice) and CLandOrdersView::OnAccept. `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section C.4, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landorders.md, section A.
